Review of 22b1c03 (wip 1.24.37: ANS in a drawing's notes is the sum just before it), against 50f9ceb.
By a reviewer who did not write it and did not read tests/notes_ans_1237.js.

Run:  git show 22b1c03:src/lantern.inner.html > /tmp/x.html; node replay.js /tmp/x.html   (run_22b1c03.txt)
      205 cases: 192 AGREE, 13 DISAGREE
      = 145 cases of the reviewer's own (132 AGREE, 13 DISAGREE) + 60 guards (all AGREE).
On 50f9ceb (before_50f9ceb.inner.html) the same cases: 99 AGREE, 106 DISAGREE -- the cases see the change.
On src/lantern.inner.html as it now stands (afea882, committed during the review): 186 AGREE, 19 DISAGREE -- the
six more are guards of saved electronics replies (an Arduino pin switching a relay through a transistor) that build
otherwise: that is afea882's change (a transistor's load), not this one.

HIGH
1. ANS1, ANS2 ... count the drawing's SUMS; Lantern's own full prompt says they count LINES.  [n-ansn-lines-vs-sums]
   The 35B's prompt (CHAT.buildSystem, full mode -- the same prompt that carries "note <text> ... Lantern works out
   each {= ...}") says "ANS holds the previous result, ANS1 the first line's, ANS2 the second's". A note line with no
   sum (a formula in words, as the 35B writes them: "note P = V*I; R = V/I; V = I*R" is in the saved replies) or with
   two sums puts the two countings apart, and Lantern takes another note's value without a word:
     note Formula: 1/Rt = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3
     note Rt = {=1/(1/10+1/15+1/30)} ohm
     note I1 = {=9/10} A
     note It = {=9/ANS2} A          -> drawn "It = 10 A" (ANS2 = sum 2 = I1's 0.9; line 2 is Rt's 5 -> 1.8 A)
   On 50f9ceb it went back (Unknown name ANS2). Rule 7: both readings are live, so the reading is not surer than the
   model. Take ANSn only where the n-th sum and the n-th note line are the same note (every note before it has exactly
   one sum); otherwise send it back with the line, naming the sum by its note ("Rt's 5 is ANS1: write {=9/ANS1}").

2. A wrong total carried by ANS gets past AI_SCHEMATIC_TOTAL's check.  [b-foreign-via-ans, b-foreign-via-ans-1-over]
   The check reads only the digits written in the total's own {= }. Question Q12 (4, 6 and 12 ohm):
     note Rt = R1 x R2 / (R1 + R2) = {=100*200/(100+200)}
     note Rt = {=ANS} ohm           -> ok=true, drawn "Rt = 66.67 ohm" beside Lantern's own "... so Rt = 2 ohm"
     note 1/Rt = {=1/100+1/200} / note Rt = {=1/ANS} ohm   -> the same, ok=true
   Written straight ("Rt = {=100*200/(100+200)} ohm") it goes back with the line to write [b-foreign-direct, AGREE].
   This is the very copy the check was built for (1.24.6: the 2B wrote the guide's 100 and 200). On 50f9ceb the first
   drew "Rt = 0 ohm" (also not sent back), the second went back as Divide by zero. Carry each sum's foreign numbers
   in the notes' state, so a sum that takes ANS or ANSn takes them too.

MEDIUM
3. ANS takes the sum just before, also when the note's own words point elsewhere; nothing is said.
   [n-ans-branch-currents, n-ans-crosses-typed-value]
     Rt = {=...} ohm / I1 = {=9/10} A / I2 = {=9/15} A / I3 = {=9/30} A / Total current It = {=9/ANS} A
       -> "Total current It = 30 A" (9 V on 5 ohm is 1.8 A), ok=true; on 50f9ceb it went back.
     P in R1 = {=9*9/10} W / Rt = 5 ohm / It = {=9/ANS} A   -> "It = 1.111 A": ANS skips the note that states Rt.
   This is ANS as the full prompt defines it ("the previous result"), so it is the model's sum as written -- but the
   small models' short prompt says nothing of ANS, and the model may mean "the answer" (small models write "ANS:" for
   ANSWER: "ANS: The battery runs for {result} h", bench_run_1244_08b.json). At least say it (rule 2): when ANS takes a sum from another note, say which ("It's ANS
   is I3's 0.3 A") in plan.said / the look turn; or question an ANS that crosses a note stating a number of its own.
4. The TOTAL check reads the digits of ANS2, ANS3 ... as numbers of the circuit.  [b-ansn-digit-not-foreign]
     R1 = {=10} ohm / R2 = {=15} ohm / R1 and R2 together = {=ANS1*ANS2/(ANS1+ANS2)} ohm
       -> sent back: "the note's sum uses 2, which are not values of this circuit, and shows 6 ohm ... Write the note
          line as ..." -- a false reason, and a right partial note to be replaced. With 10 and 15 written in, Lantern
          adds the total itself and the drawing is made. Strip the names before reading numbers
          (e.g. e.replace(/\bANS\d*\b/gi, "")) in AI_SCHEMATIC_TOTAL's foreign test.
5. A note naming the total with another number of ohms is drawn beside Lantern's total, and nothing goes back.
   [b-missing-resistor-via-ans, b-reciprocal-as-total-via-ans; b-missing-resistor-direct, low]
     1/Rt = {=1/4+1/6} / Rt = {=1/ANS} ohm      -> "Rt = 2.4 ohm" and Lantern's "Rt = 2 ohm" (went back on 50f9ceb,
                                                    as Divide by zero)
     1/Rt = {=1/10+1/15+1/30} / Rt = {=ANS} ohm -> "Rt = 0.2 ohm" and Lantern's "Rt = 5 ohm" (50f9ceb: "Rt = 0 ohm")
   Written straight it is the same (pre-existing: the check only looks for numbers that are not the circuit's). The
   change lets more of these reach the picture. A note whose words name the total (Rt, total, equivalent) and whose
   ohms are not the circuit's total could go back with Lantern's line (rule 7: the label says what it is).

LOW
6. The ANSn messages speak of Chat's lines and say nothing to write (rule 3).  [e-ansn-out-of-range-words,
   e-ansn-failed-words]  Under three note lines: "ANS3 is not a line before this one (there is 1)"; with no sum on
   line 1 and a failed sum in note 2: "ANS1 has no result: line 1 failed". Catch them in noteText and say how notes
   count ("ANS1, ANS2 ... are the drawing's first, second sum: here ANS1 is Rt's 5").
7. "It = {=9/ANS} A where Rt = {=...} ohm" after an I1 note takes I1's 0.9 -> "It = 10 A where Rt = 5 ohm".
   [n-ans-after-later-sum-same-note]
8. A note is cut at 120 characters after its sums are worked out: ANS can take a value the drawing does not show.
   [n-ans-hidden-by-cut]
9. noteText's comment says ANS "is what it is in Chat's sums and on the calculator". Chat's differs (unchanged by this
   commit, f-assist-first-ans and f-assist-skip-failed agree with 50f9ceb): Chat's first line "=ANS*30" still gives 0
   (assist.run questions ANS only when steps.length > 0 -- the 0 that 1.24.7 meant to end), and after a failed line
   Chat's ANS is the last line that worked, where the notes question it. The notes' choice is the safer; the comment
   should say they differ, and Chat's first-line 0 is for the queue.

Seen, outside this change (no case is about it): a sheet's "=ANS+1" is 1 (Excel: #NAME?) [f-sheet-ans pins the
50f9ceb value]; a note's 0.0005 is drawn "0.0005000" (fmt keeps toPrecision's zeros) [m-ele-lower pins it]; with 8 notes
of the model's, Lantern's added total note is the ninth and is not drawn [b-ninth-note shows 8].

WHAT AGREES
- Adam's laptop reply: noteText, built (alone, and with prose around it), and the bench loop in one round: "Rt = ... = 5
  ohm", "Total current It = 1.8 A", no problems. [n-adam-35b, b-adam-35b-block, b-adam-35b-block-prose, s-bench-one-round]
- Right notes: chains, two or three sums in a note, lowercase ans/Ans, spaces, ANS*ANS, SQRT/ROUND/% of ANS, ANS(),
  full precision (1/3 then *3 is 1), negative, PI, CONVERT then area, Ohm sign, quoted notes, a text note between, ANS1/
  ANS2 where each note has one sum, series current and voltage, LED power, the 12 V lesson's current, a lamp's power,
  text and label lines, notes before the parts.
- Never 0: ANS with no sum before (alone, Rt = {=ANS}, reversed order, reversed in one note), after a failed sum, after
  a text result, twice: "?" and "uses ANS, the sum worked out just before it, but there is no sum before it: write the
  number, or its own sum, in place of ANS" -- said once, sent back whole by the bench, no "Divide by zero".
- Not ANS: ANSWER, ANSI, BANS, ANS_1, "ANS 1", 2ANS, ANS(2), ANS100, ANS in quotes -- as on 50f9ceb.
- One state per drawing: built twice; the next drawing, the next module (hydraulic then pneumatic, wheel then
  schematic); the TOTAL pass then the draw pass (a reversed ANS stays questioned, a chain is not advanced twice); two
  blocks in one reply (aiAct.rest, and Chat's moreMade); the bench's second try (fresh, and computed after another fault).
  A caller with no state: each note alone.
- Every module that shows notes: AI_HYDRAULIC, AI_PNEUMATIC, AI_CONTROL, AI_ELECTRONICS, AI_WHEEL (note/key/caption, 6
  notes), AI_SCHEMATIC_MORE (8 notes): ANS after a sum worked out, ANS first questioned, ANSn, after a failed sum.
- The engine's own ANS elsewhere as on 50f9ceb: assist.run, formula.evaluate (ans, ansList, ANS1 with none), a sheet,
  the calculator (2+3= then ANS x 2 = 10).
- Guards: all 555 saved replies with a MAKE block in tests/fixtures/bench_run*.json (59 files) build exactly as on
  50f9ceb on 22b1c03 -- ok, problems, notes as drawn and the whole plan; the 150 + 150 bench prompts (aiAct.prompt,
  CHAT.buildSystem full and short; sets A and B) are unchanged.

NOT RUN
- No model: no bench run on the laptop or on GitHub; every reply here is written by the reviewer or saved.
- No real browser (Playwright): jsdom only (load.js). npm test not run, as asked.
- The look turn with a picture (canSee is false in jsdom); the Draw app; MAKE STATION and the float drawings (they do
  not work out sums at all).
- Cases were not run against a model's real ANSn notes: none of the 81 saved runs has ANS in a note.
